Correlations and relationships

Source: vignettes/correlations-and-relationships.Rmd
correlations-and-relationships.Rmd
library(golfops)
sample <- dobson_operating_daily()
played <- sample[!is.na(sample$rounds_played) & sample$rounds_played > 0, ]
categories <- c(
  "Total revenue" = "total_revenue",
  "Green fees" = "green_fee_revenue",
  "Food and beverage" = "food_beverage_revenue",
  "Merchandise" = "merchandise_revenue",
  "Range" = "range_revenue",
  "Cart" = "cart_revenue",
  "Club rental" = "club_revenue"
)
revenue_correlation <- function(block) {
  round(vapply(categories, function(column) {
    stats::cor(block$rounds_played, block[[column]], use = "complete.obs")
  }, numeric(1)), 2)
}

Each number is the correlation of golfers with that day’s recorded revenue, on days with at least one golfer. The charts below are the same days. Each point is one day. The horizontal axis is golfers, and the line is a straight fit to that year’s days. These are associations. They are not evidence that an extra golfer causes the extra spending, and they are not a price.

Correlation of golfers with each daily revenue amount. * 2021 and 2026 are half years: 2021 is July through December, and 2026 is January through April.

Each section is one calendar year. A panel uses that revenue type’s color, the same colors as the annual revenue bars. 2021 starts on July 1, and the latest year ends with the extract.
